claims.statement: The `topos` root CLI dispatches ten public routes: config, evaluate, inspect, compare, coverage, depgraph, install, uninstall, status, and mcp; each routes to its corresponding command handler and command errors terminate with exit status 1.

CLI evaluation can recurse and filter discovered languages, has JSON, verbose, info, failures, and priority controls, rejects `--json` combined with `--info` or `--failures`, and uses priority to select classification/remediation ordering.

The CLI and MCP evaluation routes share an ensure policy for COMPOSABLE: unless skipped, they resolve GitNexus state and attempt generation for missing, stale, branch-not-indexed, or load-error stores; failures leave evaluation available without COMPOSABLE rather than failing the whole evaluation.

A GitNexus override derives the COMPOSABLE project root from the store parent and must be resolved before reuse to avoid relative-path double joins; the MCP-specific root resolver prevents an override outside the file root from being used.

`topos depgraph generate` is a CLI wrapper around dependency-graph generation that no-ops for a current graph unless forced and refuses a schema-mismatched store; the MCP status tool is read-only while generation is the side-effecting counterpart.

The stdio server combines evaluate, assess, compare, coverage, depgraph, docs, inspect, preferences, and refactor routers, and advertises tool, resource, and prompt capabilities including documentation resources, a build resource, and the `topos_refactor_until_ideal` prompt.

Topos explicitly supports MCP revisions from 2024-11-05 through 2026-07-28; lifecycle tests exercise initialize/initialized and stateless `server/discover`, and show that the latter supplies protocol metadata per request while the tool surface stays the same.

MCP file access resolves a project using `.git`, `pyproject.toml`, or `Cargo.toml`; `TOPOS_MCP_FILE_ROOT`, when set, is a maximum boundary, and calls reject paths outside it or requests with no detectable project marker.

The assessment family distinguishes explicit side-by-side variants, Git-ref worktree comparisons, pre-edit snapshots, snapshot assessment, and multi-file changesets; worktree assessment reads the baseline from Git, while snapshots are required for uncommitted or untracked baselines.

Assessments compare lattice status and score deltas and compute normalized AST distance when both sources parse; an otherwise improving result becomes `SUSPICIOUS_NO_STRUCTURAL_CHANGE` when distance is below 0.02 and a score delta has magnitude at least 3.0.

Refactor snapshots are on-disk, content-addressed records outside the working tree, survive a server restart, can be relocated with `TOPOS_SNAPSHOT_DIR`, and expire after 24 hours; malformed, missing, or expired identifiers are returned as blocked snapshot outcomes.

Security diagnostic overlays are only constructed for parseable classifications that fail dangerous-call or taint-flow metrics; allowlist handling partitions raw findings into active and acknowledged risks rather than removing allowed findings before disclosure and verdict adjustment.

Structural coverage and advisory refactor analysis are explicitly separate from the four-pillar quality lattice: coverage uses UAST declaration matching and k-gram recall without running tests, while refactor ranks hotspots without scoring pillars.

With no `--language` filter, `topos evaluate` discovers every supported source suffix and detects each file's language; an explicit existing file with an unsupported suffix or one excluded by `--language` is an error rather than a silent omission, while missing paths are reported separately.

CLI evaluation treats COMPOSABLE as optional: `--no-composable` skips MDG resolution, and a failure to resolve or load the GitNexus dependency graph produces warnings while classification continues without the COMPOSABLE representation.

MCP evaluation tool annotations distinguish pure snippet evaluation from file/project evaluation that may prepare `.gitnexus`: `topos_evaluate_code` is read-only, while `topos_evaluate_file` and `topos_evaluate_project` are non-read-only and may generate or refresh COMPOSABLE state without editing source.

`topos_evaluate_project` recursively discovers all supported source files, detects a language per file, returns per-language rollups and a weakest-file floor, and paginates the sorted file rows using bounded `limit` and `offset` values.

For in-place MCP assessment, `topos_assess_worktree_change` reads the baseline from a Git ref and defaults that ref to `HEAD`; a dash-prefixed ref is rejected before invoking Git, so dirty or untracked baselines instead require the pre-edit snapshot route.

The MCP lifecycle contract is exercised through real stdio JSON-RPC frames: initialize-era clients negotiate a pinned supported revision and use `notifications/initialized`, while the stateless `server/discover` flow supplies protocol metadata on every request and exposes the same tool list.

Baseline snapshots are persisted outside the working tree in a per-project temporary-store namespace by default (overridable with `TOPOS_SNAPSHOT_DIR`), use a content-addressed ID derived from filepath and source hash, survive MCP server restarts, and expire after 24 hours.

`topos inspect` applies the same optional GitNexus preparation policy as CLI evaluation; in text mode an unparseable input prints a parse-failure summary and exits nonzero, while JSON mode emits the inspection payload.
